changes.subject: Opaque trailer severity
changes.before: Generic high-entropy/executable stowaway plus a >=64KiB PNG trailer became hostile when whole-file size reached 500,000 bytes.
changes.after: The actual trailing region must classify as high_entropy; the finding is suspicious independently of whole-file size. Large opaque trailers do not prove malicious content.

changes.subject: Trailer location
changes.before: The generic media.stowaway list combined freeform metadata, interior gaps and trailing data, so a header in metadata could be falsely attributed to a text trailer.
changes.after: New media.trailing_content_kind retains the classification of the actual trailing region without reclassifying it or changing existing stowaway coverage. Neutral location-specific metadata facts let rules refer to it.

changes.subject: Executable trailer claim
changes.before: A PNG with an unrelated executable header and ordinary trailer was described as a trailer that parses as an executable and labeled hostile.
changes.after: The rule requires an executable header in the trailing region, reports exactly a header, and is suspicious. Fully parsed PE/ELF images reconstructed from pixels still retain hostile findings.

changes.subject: Probe limits
changes.after: New notable finding png-pixel-payload-probe-limited makes bounded scanning explicit; zero recovered payloads is not presented as an exhaustive clearance.

changes.subject: Readability
changes.after: IEND findings say CRC-correct records; container-problem wording does not imply that an image cannot render. Comments no longer state that every consumer ignores extra bytes or that all large tails are payloads.

anti_evasion: One or several forged IEND records do not suppress or lower a suspicious trailer. Covered metadata and interior program headers do not become program-trailer facts.

new_adversarial_controls: Executable header in metadata with an ordinary long text trailer
Large opaque trailer followed by multiple forged CRC-correct IENDs
